editorial:
If you enjoy grounded military thrillers with a strong emotional core, The Contractor is a solid pick. Chris Pine plays James Harper, a Special Forces soldier forced out of the military who takes a risky private contracting job to support his family. Alongside his best friend Mike, played by Ben Foster, and under veteran commander Rusty, played by Kiefer Sutherland, Harper heads overseas on a covert mission that quickly falls apart. The setup feels personal and tense, and the movie keeps you invested in Harper's struggle to survive and get back home to his wife and son.

The action is gritty and realistic rather than flashy, and Pine delivers a believable, weary performance that carries the film. Foster and Sutherland add strong support, and the pacing stays steady with a few genuinely tense set pieces. On the downside, the plot can feel familiar if you have seen other soldier-turned-contractor stories, and some twists are easy to guess. Still, it is an engaging watch for fans of grounded action.
endingExplained: Harper discovers the mission was a setup. Rusty planned to steal the scientist Salim's research for profit and had Harper's team ambushed. Mike is killed during the betrayal, but Harper protects Salim and fights off Rusty's men. In the final scenes, Harper confronts the conspiracy, survives the shootout, and makes it home. He embraces his wife and son, choosing to leave the contracting life behind and focus on his family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves military thrillers and Chris Pine action movies.
